newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip on back of Probanka fall.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip on back of Probanka fall.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.17 percent on Monday, pulled down by bank Probanka as it fell prey to a technical correction.

Traders expect the market to show little movement with trading volume remaining at a low ebb until parliament votes on whether to ratify the association agreement with the European Union, which is expected to happen next week.

"If parliament ratifies the agreement that could push shares up by some 10 percent in the week following that as it would give a welcome signal to foreign investors and could lure some fresh foreign investment to the market," one trader said.
The SBI index fell 2.3 points to 1,321.03.
Probanka shed 3.37 percent after gaining 3.9 percent last week. It closed at 20,100 tolars on volume of 1,000 shares and was the day's leading decliner.
Traders said Probanka may have bottomed out as its price seemed low compared to its business results and prospects.
Overall six shares fell, seven rose and 15 were untraded. Turnover eased to 44.8 million tolars from 46.1 million.
Bank UBK was the top gainer, up 9.74 percent to 7,550 tolars on volume of 110 shares, pushed up by Thursday's news that Slovenia's second largest bank SKB would buy 51 percent of UBK in June.
Since the news UBK has jumped 19.8 percent and traders said it could reach 10,000 tolars in the next 10 days as the link-up with SKB is expected to ease UBK's liquidity problems.
